items.t: Says she will continue to prioritize fiscal responsibility during her second term.
items.q: will continue to prioritize fiscal responsibility, affordable healthcare and early childhood development during her time in office.

items.t: Was against the proposed amendment to change the Kansas state constitution on abortion (2022).
items.q: She opposed the proposed amendment, saying changing the state constitution would “throw the state back into the Dark Ages.”

items.t: Proposed an executive reorganization order creating the Kansas Department of Human Services, which would include the current programs of the Department for Children and Families and the Department for Aging and Disability Services.
items.q: Governor Laura Kelly today announced her intent to once again submit an executive reorganization order (ERO) to the Kansas Legislature creating the Kansas Department of Human Services (KDHS). The new agency will include the current programs at the Department for Children and Families (DCF) and the Department for Aging and Disability Services (KDADS).

record.t: Was re-elected and sworn in for a second term as the 48th Governor of Kansas.
record.q: Governor Laura Kelly was re-elected and sworn in for a second term as the 48th Governor of the State of Kansas on January 9, 2023.

record.t: Issued a state of emergency moments after announcing Kansas's first coronavirus-related death.
record.q: Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly announced at a Thursday news conference, according to the Topeka Capital-Journal. She issued a state of emergency moments later.

record.t: Served as 48th Governor of Kansas starting in January 2019.
record.q: Served as 48th Governor of Kansas: January 14, 2019, to present.

record.t: Was elected Governor of Kansas in 2018 with Lynn Rogers as lieutenant governor.
record.q: She was elected to be the third woman to serve as Kansas governor in 2018 with Lynn Rogers as lieutenant governor.

record.t: Served in the Kansas Senate, 18th district, from January 2005 to January 2019.
record.q: Served in the Kansas Senate, 18th district: January 3, 2005 – January 2019.

record.t: Served as assistant minority leader and minority whip in the Kansas Senate.
record.q: Reelected three times, she served as assistant minority leader and minority whip.

record.t: Vetoed House Sub for SB 244, which requires designation of multi-occupancy spaces in public buildings for use by only one sex; the House and Senate overrode the veto.
record.q: The bill passed out of the Kansas House and Senate, was vetoed by Gov. Laura Kelly and then her veto was overridden by the House and Senate.
